paper.title_en: Bogoliubov excitations of a Bose-Einstein condensate in the presence of the non-Hermitian skin effect
paper.abstract_en: The non-Hermitian skin effect is one of the most remarkable topological features of non-conservative physics. It causes a macroscopic accumulation of states at the boundaries of a confined system, opening new ways for controlling and directing waves in non-Hermitian settings. The non-Hermitian skin effect has recently been observed in experiments with Bose-Einstein condensates of exciton polaritons and ultracold bosonic quantum gases. Here, we develop a non-Hermitian extension of the Bogoliubov-de-Gennes theory for the collective excitations of the condensate, both in the semiclassical (mean-field) and second-quantised framework. By considering a trapped condensate under the action of an imaginary gauge field, we find that while the repulsive interactions oppose the localisation of the condensate, its excitations continue to display a strong skin effect. As a consequence, in the presence of harmonic confinement, we predict a strong shift in the dipole oscillation frequency, in contrast to Hermitian systems, where this frequency is fixed by the trap dimensions. Furthermore, we find that a second-quantised treatment removes the shift of the dipole oscillation frequency entirely. The two approaches describe different physical regimes, and identifying which one a given platform realises requires a microscopic open-system description. We suggest that this discrepancy between the two theoretical approaches can be resolved in experiments.
